summary: Help and the Tutorials window offer a Video track again at Next. Its six guides open a practice recording in the editor and walk you through cutting it down, adding a second clip, a moving title, a transition, captions and export, using Premiere's keys.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Help, Tutorials, Video, Cut a recording down. Follow it: Q, W, Command K, then Delete.
Run Add a second clip and drag b-roll from the Media shelf onto the end of V1.
Run A title that moves: press T, type a title, press Command Return, click the Position diamond, then drag the title a second later.
Run Put a transition on a cut, click the cut and pick Cross dissolve.
Run Captions from the speech, wait for the captions, then double click one on the picture and fix a word.
Run Export the video and press Shift Command E.

evaluate: Would someone who knows Premiere recognise Q, W, Command K and Delete as the way to cut here, or would they reach for the Blade first?
Is the card over the middle of the timeline in the right place, or does it hide the clip you are being asked to work on?
Does the cut guide move on at the right moments, only after you really trim or cut?
Are six short guides the right size, or would you rather have one longer video guide that makes a whole edit?
Is anything a first-time video editor needs missing from the track, such as detaching the sound or changing a clip's speed?
rough: The first frame of every recording is drawn blurry until the playhead moves. It shows on every guide's first card. Filed as its own task.
Opening a recording puts the Trim tool in hand, so its In, Out and Trim bar floats over the picture through guides that never use it.
The card sits over the middle of the floating tool bar while it points at the timeline.
A clip brought in from the shelf shows no waveform under its sound on the Audio track. Filed as its own task.
The mock's cut walkthrough uses the Blade and Detach Audio. The guide teaches Q, W and Command K instead, because those need no tool change and the Blade is not on the video tool bar yet.

The walks land b-roll with V1 picked and Add at Playhead, the card's second way, not by dragging, because a timeline drop has not been watched with the screen locked yet. The drag itself is covered by the second clip walks.
The captions guide needs the Mac's speech recognition. Where that is missing, the first card promises captions that never arrive.
